318242.title: The Zero-in-the-Spectrum conjecture
318242.statement: Let $\widetilde{M}$ be a complete Riemannian manifold and suppose it is the universal covering of an aspherical closed Riemannian manifold $M$, with the metric induced from $M$. Let $\Delta_p$ be the Laplacian on smooth $p$-forms, and let $(\Delta_p)_{\min}$ denote its minimal closure on $L^2\Omega^p(\widetilde{M})$. **Zero-in-the-Spectrum conjecture.** For some $p\geq0$, zero belongs to the spectrum of $(\Delta_p)_{\min}$. The conjecture concerns spectral behavior of Laplacians on universal covers of closed aspherical manifolds; the source records non-aspherical counterexamples, which do not refute the stated aspherical version.

320386.title: Wojciechowski–Keller volume-boundary conjecture for stochastic completeness
320386.statement:
Let $(V,E)$ be a graph, choose a fixed root $x^*\in V$, and let $B_r$ be the ball of radius $r$ about $x^*$. Let $\partial B_r$ denote its outer vertex boundary, and write $\#A$ for the cardinality of a finite set $A$. **Wojciechowski–Keller conjecture.** If

$$
\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}\frac{\#B_r}{\#\partial B_r}=+\infty,
$$

then $(V,E)$ is stochastically complete.

This conjecture gives a volume-to-boundary criterion for stochastic completeness. The supplied status evidence says that Bär and Bessa constructed a counterexample to Grigor'yan's conjecture; accordingly, this statement is refuted.

321442.title: Conjecture on unions of intersecting strictly informative groves
321442.statement:
Let two groves be **strictly informative** if each satisfies the strict informativeness criterion for determining supertrees. Let the groves be collections of taxon sets, with intersection and union taken as collections of taxon sets. **Strictly informative grove union conjecture.** The union of two intersecting strictly informative groves is a grove.

This is proposed as a weaker statement related to the earlier conjecture on groves. The paper gives a counterexample showing that the union of two intersecting strictly informative groves need not itself be strictly informative, even when it is a grove; the conjecture asserts only the weaker grove property.
321442.review_depth: primary rooted-tree definitions, conjecture and neighbouring proofs read; multiple exact bounded searches
321442.primary_scope: A topology assignment may depend on the partition. A grove requires either no cross triple or some informative compatible rooted-tree assignment for EVERY nontrivial partition. Strictly informative requires the latter for every such partition. Intersection is as collections of taxon sets.
321442.mathematical_attempt: Enumerated all rooted binary supertrees on 4,5,6 taxa and projected them to input taxon sets. Compatible assignments are restriction-signature classes. A cross triple is resolved iff its rooted resolution is constant in such a class. Exhaustive family classifications and union tests are in logs/groves.log. Mixed 3/4-element taxon sets on six taxa gave 1100 strictly informative families of size 2..4 after a necessary private-taxon filter; 5000 sampled intersecting pairs passed. Seven-taxon bitset computation used all 10395 rooted binary trees, classified 3000 sampled private-taxon families, found 1277 distinct strict families and tested 1000 intersecting pairs without a witness. Full six-taxon all-pairs extension hit the wall cap and is NOT credited as complete.
321442.remaining_gap: No general union lemma or counterexample. Need control of resolved triples when a partition of the union masks cross triples of either constituent. Small family tests cannot supply that bridge. The source Remark 3.19 example itself fails the stated strict criterion in our diagnostic; it is an adjacent source defect, not a solution of Conjecture 3.13.

323969.title: Fleischner's conjecture on compatible cycle decompositions
323969.statement:
Let $G$ be an essentially $6$-edge-connected $4$-regular graph with a **transition system** $T$. A compatible cycle decomposition is a cycle decomposition compatible with the transitions prescribed by $T$.

325862.title: Hof–Knill–Simon conjecture on palindromic fixed points and conjugates in class P
325862.statement:
Let ${\bf u}$ be the fixed point of a primitive morphism. An infinite sequence is **palindromic** if it contains an infinite number of palindrome factors.

**Hof–Knill–Simon conjecture.** ${\bf u}$ is palindromic if and only if there exists a morphism $\varphi\neq\operatorname{Id}$ such that

$$
\varphi({\bf u})={\bf u}
$$

and $\varphi$ has a conjugate in class $\mathcal P$.

This conjecture was reformulated from the original question of Hof, Knill and Simon about whether every palindromic fixed point arises from a substitution in an extended version of class $\mathcal P$. The paper gives a counterexample on a ternary alphabet, so the conjecture is refuted.

325862.remaining_gap: No new endpoint; a bounded palindrome search would not certify an infinite-palindrome or all-morphisms statement and is unnecessary after the exact known refutation.

326960.title: The trap bound for restricted cop number in diameter-two graphs
326960.statement:
Let $G$ be a diameter-$2$ graph, let $H\subseteq G$ be a subgraph, and let $c_G(H)$ denote the least number of ordinary cops needed to catch a robber restricted to $H$, while the cops may move along all edges of $G$. Call $H$ an $s$-trap when the robber can be caught under the corresponding trap condition with parameter $s$.

**Restricted cop-number trap conjecture.** If $H$ is an $s$-trap in $G$, then

$$
c_G(H)\leq s.
$$

The paper says this conjecture could be used to improve the upper bounds, but gives no proof or counterexample.

327368.title: The index-invariance conjecture for generalized Fibonacci cubes
327368.statement:
Let $f$ and $f'$ be binary strings, and let $Q_d(f)$ denote the generalized Fibonacci cube obtained by forbidding $f$. Let $\nu(f)$ denote the index of the binary word $f$, as defined in the paper. A pair $f,f'$ is **non-trivial** if neither string is obtained from the other by complementation, reversal, or a composition of these mappings.

**Index-invariance conjecture.** If $f,f'$ are a non-trivial pair such that

$$
Q_d(f)\cong Q_d(f'),
$$

then

$$
\nu(f)=\nu(f').
$$

The paper notes that equality of indices is sufficient for isomorphism in a particular long-forbidden-word case but not in general, giving a counterexample when $|f|=|f'|\leq d-2$. The conjecture proposes the converse invariant for non-trivial isomorphic pairs.

All forbidden-word orbits under reversal/complement, 3 <= length < d, were screened through dimension 11 with no cross-nu invariant collision. Attempted dimension 12 hit wall cap; no complete dimension-12 coverage from that run. A separate vectorized canonical color-refinement implementation COMPLETED dimensions 4..12 with no cross-index collisions; dimension 12 covered 1083 reversal/complement orbit representatives. This supersedes only the coverage limit, not the killed-run receipts.

327764.title: Lauritzen's score matching estimability conjecture
327764.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph with $m$ vertices, and let $n$ be the sample dimension. The graph is **$n$-estimable** when its score matching estimator exists with probability one.

328930.title: Higher-dimensional generalization of the good-spacing conjecture
328930.statement:
Let $A\subseteq[1,n]\times[1,n]$ satisfy $|A|=\delta n^2$. **Higher-dimensional good-spacing conjecture.** There exist constants $c_1,c_2,c_3>0$ depending only on $\delta$ and a subset $A'\subseteq A$ with $|A'|\geq c_1|A|$ such that, for $c_2n^2$ pairs of integers $0\leq i,j\leq n/c_3$,

$$
\left|A'\cap[0,ic_3)\times[0,jc_3)\right|=ij.
$$

This is proposed as a higher-dimensional analogue of the paper's good-spacing statement, concerning subsets that are well distributed in many intervals or rectangles. The source describes it as tentative and notes that finding a counterexample would also be interesting.
328930.review_depth: primary exact Conjecture 17 and preceding good-spacing context read
328930.primary_scope: For each positive density delta, constants c1,c2,c3 depend ONLY on delta, uniformly in n and the dense grid subset.
328930.mathematical_attempt: The one-dimensional selection argument does not preserve both coordinate prefix counts after tensoring or selecting rows separately. The two-dimensional equality is an exact integer prefix-count condition. No finite n can disprove existence of arbitrary density-dependent constants.
328930.remaining_gap: Need an asymptotic dense obstruction family defeating every constants choice, or a uniform simultaneous prefix-count selection theorem. A fixed-grid diagnostic is not a finite decision procedure for this conjecture.

329633.title: Akbari–Mohammadian–Radjavi–Raja's commuting graph diameter conjecture

331024.title: Keleti's perimeter-to-area conjecture for unions of unit squares
331024.statement:

$$
\frac{P(U)}{A(U)}\leq 4.
$$

334189.title: The decomposition conjecture for extremal 2-increasing sequences
334189.statement:
Let $T$ be a 2-increasing sequence in $[r]\times[s]\times[t]$.

**Decomposition conjecture for extremal 2-increasing sequences.**

$$
|T|\le (rst)^{1/2},
$$

and equality holds only if there is a decomposition of the kind discussed in the paper for some choice of label coordinate.

The conjecture is motivated by all known examples attaining the bound, which admit such a decomposition. The paper gives a non-decomposable example that is not extremal, so it does not refute the conjecture; the extremal equality case remains unresolved.

337196.title: The PFR conjecture over \d8352\d8357 and \d8357\d8357: GAP formulation
337196.statement:
Let $G = \mathbb{R}^m$ or $\mathbb{Z}^m$, and let $A \subseteq G$ be finite with $|A+A| \leq K|A|$. A generalized arithmetic progression is a set

$$
P = \big\{a_0+n_1a_1+\dots+n_da_d: n_i \in \{0,\dots,N_i-1\}\big\}.
$$

**PFR conjecture, GAP formulation.** There should exist such a progression $P$, with $a_i \in G$, rank $d = O(\log 2K)$ and size $O(K^{O(1)})|A|$, together with a set $X \subseteq G$ of size $O(K^{O(1)})$, such that $A \subseteq P+X$. This formulation is a natural polynomial quantitative version of Freiman-type structure theorems, but it is false: Lovett and Regev produced a counterexample in $\mathbb{R}^m$, answering a question of Green.

340435.title: Lovász and Szegedy's finite-dimension conjecture for typical vertices
340435.statement: A **graphon** is a measurable symmetric function $W:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$. It is **finitely forcible** if it is uniquely determined, up to weak isomorphism, by the densities of finitely many graphs. Each graphon has an associated topological space whose points correspond to types of vertices appearing in sequences of graphs converging to it; these points are called typical vertices. **Lovász and Szegedy's finite-dimension conjecture.** The space of typical vertices of every finitely forcible graphon has finite dimension. This conjecture was disproved by a counterexample construction, so the space of typical vertices of a finitely forcible graphon can have infinite dimension.

340435.primary_scope: Topological space of typical vertices of finitely forcible graphons; arbitrary dimension, not dimensions of finite graph approximations.
340435.mathematical_attempt: Downloaded Glebov-Klimosova-Kral 1404.2743. Proposition 5 embeds a countable product [0,1]^N in typical-vertex spaces via the D-part coordinate map; Theorem 6 proves finite forcibility, giving Theorem 1. The 2020 source also explicitly records this resolution.

340468.title: Lovász's stronger Ryser conjecture
340468.statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be an $r$-partite hypergraph, let $\nu(\mathcal{H})$ be its matching number, and for a set $S$ of vertices let $\mathcal{H}-S$ denote the hypergraph obtained by deleting $S$ and all incident edges.

**Lovász's stronger Ryser conjecture.** There exists a set $S$ of vertices with $|S|\leq r-1$ such that

$$
\nu(\mathcal{H}-S)\leq \nu(\mathcal{H})-1.
$$

A negative answer to the preceding problem about intersecting Ryser subhypergraphs would disprove this stronger version of Ryser's conjecture. The source presents it as a stronger conjectural statement and does not give a resolution.
340468.review_depth: original conjecture, exact finite sweeps and 2025 primary counterexample theorem/proof mechanism read
340468.primary_scope: Nonempty r-partite r-uniform hypergraph, delete at most r-1 vertices to reduce matching number. Empty-hypergraph wording defects are not counted.
340468.mathematical_attempt: Early exact sweeps: all 255 nonempty subhypergraphs of K(2,2,2), all 65535 nonempty subhypergraphs of K(2,2,2,2), and 10000 seeded samples in K(3,3,3), no witness. Live search then found Clow-Haxell-Mohar 2505.05339: line hypergraph of the Biggs-Smith graph gives an r=3 counterexample. Read Theorem 1.3 and line-hypergraph/independence bridge and Section 3 proof portions. Successor 2506.21286 supplies infinite families.

340641.title: Amdeberhan's root conjecture for Nekrasov–Okounkov polynomials
340641.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition of $n$, and let $\mathcal{H}(\lambda)$ be its multiset of hook lengths. For a positive integer $n$, define

$$
Q_n(z):=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\prod_{h\in\mathcal{H}(\lambda)}\left(\frac{h^2+z}{h^2}\right)\in\mathbb{C}[z].
$$

**Amdeberhan's root conjecture.** The polynomial $Q_n(z)$ has (i) only simple roots, (ii) only real roots, and (iii) only negative roots. The polynomial is considered in connection with the roots arising from the Nekrasov–Okounkov hook length formula and the Lehmer conjecture. The paper gives a counterexample to part (ii), and consequently part (iii) must also be revised; hence the conjunction of the three assertions is refuted.
340641.review_depth: literal hook polynomial, source recurrence and rigorous counterexample proof read
340641.primary_scope: All positive n; conjunction of simplicity, realness, negativity of every root of Q_n(z).
340641.mathematical_attempt: The exact source rewrites Q_n(z)=P_n(z+1) using the hook formula and computes P_n by x/n times the sigma-weighted recurrence. P_10 has a nonreal pair; the paper gives an algebraic total-nonnegativity obstruction using a negative 26-by-26 Toeplitz minor, plus a derivative argument. This already refutes the conjunction.
340641.remaining_gap: No novel endpoint; no need to search or formalize the known n=10 witness for discovery credit.
